title: 27D to 11D compactification loop is not uniquely invertible
description: The product ansatz M27 = M11 x K16 is a Kaluza-Klein form, not a derivation from E8 (dimension 8) or from m = hf/c^2. Integrating out K16 yields an effective 11D action. Reconstructing K16 from a Laplace spectrum {lambda_n} is not unique: isospectral manifolds exist. Setting lambda_n = f_n^2 and m_n = h f_n / c^2 assigns masses to modes; it does not return the same metric.
stop_reason: decompact(compact(M27)) = M27 holds only if K16 is named again on the way back. Close this STOP only with a uniqueness theorem that reconstructs the metric of K16 from the named spectrum, or drop the 27D factor as arithmetic (11+16) without geometry.
definitions: Compactification here: integrate a 16-dimensional fibre to obtain an effective 11D action.
Spectral reconstruction: recover a Riemannian metric from Laplace eigenvalues.
27 is not the dimension of E8 and is not forced by 11D supergravity.
equations: m_n = h f_n / c^2 does not invert the fibre metric
assumptions: 11D is used as the M-theory dimension (HYP frame), not as an established spacetime.
Isospectral non-isometric manifolds exist in dimension >= 16 as in lower-dimensional examples.
mechanism: Keep 11D as a symbolic frame. Do not hydrate a closed 27 <-> 11 loop in the catalog until uniqueness is proved.
falsification_conditions: A theorem that the named {f_n} determines K16 up to isometry.
A derivation of 16 and 27 from E8 or from m = hf/c^2 without adding them by hand.
confusion_guard: 11 + 16 = 27 is arithmetic. E8 lives in 8 dimensions. A picture of two glowing manifolds is not a compactification proof.
primary_sources: Milnor, Eigenvalues of the Laplace operator on certain manifolds
predictions: Different fibres can share a spectrum and disagree on metric.
Mode masses from m = hf/c^2 will not select one K16.
